clue.text: Pays Colonel Short to play music

indicators.note: letters put into play are moved about and rearranged

parts.note: Col is the short form of Colonel, as in Col. Mustard

explanation.surface: A colonel named Short pays a band to play some music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like the colonel's surname, but it says to shorten Colonel to COL.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a style of West Indian song with a syncopated rhythm, so it is a kind of music.

clue.text: Sailor's new love let off the hook

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor, with the 's added

indicators.note: a new version of love has its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor's fresh romance that lets him escape trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from blame or guilt, which is the idiom let off the hook.

clue.text: Immature guy on rocky road

indicators.note: a rocky road jolts whatever travels on it, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the two words read together

explanation.surface: A callow fellow is heading down a difficult path in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Young describes someone at an early stage of life, not yet fully mature.

clue.text: Hornets fly around prune

indicators.note: insects that fly around dart in every direction, so the letters scatter

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wasps buzz around a dried plum.
explanation.walkthrough: Prune looks like the fruit the hornets are drawn to; it is the verb meaning cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune is to cut back or trim, which makes something shorter.

clue.text: Average disturbance unknown: it's a contradiction in terms

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
ado is fuss or commotion
x is the classic unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An everyday disturbance of no known cause is called self-contradictory.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself, which is what a contradiction in terms is.

clue.text: Trojan hero at ease, an unusual version

indicators.note: an unusual version of something is a changed form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A retelling shows a Trojan warrior relaxed for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At ease' reads as one phrase, but at is only a link and the fodder starts at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeneas fled burning Troy and is the hero of Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Article about bad apple the French pursued unaccompanied

indicators.note: the French word comes after the rest, chasing it

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
c is short for circa, about

indicators.note: a bad apple is spoilt, so its letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: la is the French feminine for the

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a bad apple, chased by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the short C for circa here, not CA; 'pursued' puts LA at the end, after the jumbled fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is performed with voices alone, without instrumental accompaniment.

clue.text: Make a pig of oneself when recovering from East Asian trip, initially

parts.note: to be over an illness is to have got past it

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs themselves on getting home from an Asian holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to eat too much, gorging greedily like a pig.

clue.text: Earn a lot from success with article on sailor's vessel

parts.note: a hit is a success
the definite article
Jack, or jack tar, is a sailor
a pot is a container

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fortune from a hit piece about a sailor's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' works as a down-clue placement: the article sits above the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the jackpot is an idiom for winning or making a large sum of money.

clue.text: Jacob's brother in Charlie's Aunt

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their join

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the possessive and the next word

explanation.surface: A Bible figure is spotted in the farce Charley's Aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Charley's Aunt is a famous Victorian stage farce, so the clue reads like a casting note.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau is the elder twin of Jacob, who tricked him out of his birthright.

clue.text: Adjust to new date, remaining correctly aligned

parts.note: to orient yourself is to adjust to new surroundings

indicators.note: a date that is being remade has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shifting an appointment to a new date, staying properly lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remaining' is read as re-maining, remade, turning DATE into ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something orientated has been set facing the right direction, that is, properly positioned.

clue.text: Get off ! It's flaming hot!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to step down from a vehicle or horse

explanation.surface: Someone yells to a passenger to get out because something is on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means dismount; as an adjective it means burning or set on fire.

clue.text: Walked over pupil — completely crushed

indicators.note: walking over something means covering it, so one word is wrapped around another

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily or a long way
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A schoolchild has been walked over and utterly squashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walked over' looks like the definition, but over is the wrapping signal; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampled describes something stamped down underfoot, so flattened or crushed.

clue.text: Ease an age problem in part of the Med

indicators.note: a problem leaves things in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters before the indicator

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean holiday spot promises relief for the troubles of growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean Sea lies between Greece and Turkey and is an arm of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Imported from outside

definitions.meaning: first meaning: brought in from elsewhere, not native
second meaning: originating or acting externally

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts read as one phrase about imports, but each alone gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrinsic means not belonging to the essential nature of a thing, coming from or operating outside it.

clue.text: Quiet US city to produce philosopher

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for soft
LA is Los Angeles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A calm American city sets out to turn out a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Athenian thinker, pupil of Socrates and author of the Republic.

clue.text: Decline and Fall?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to lessen or die down
second meaning: to drop or subside

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals and question mark summon Gibbon's Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire; here the two words are each a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm or fever that abates diminishes in strength, so it both declines and falls off.

clue.text: Reading code badly in bare, rough environment

indicators.note: the word for badly goes in the jumbled letters
the jumbled bare forms the surroundings for the inserted word
rough here means roughly put together, so the letters of bare are jumbled

parts.note: ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Learning to read some code badly in a bare, harsh setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' is not part of the scene but a second container word: the jumbled bare is the setting the inserted word sits in.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is the raised-dot system that lets blind people read by touch, a code for reading.

clue.text: A rest disturbed after foundation shows a level of interest

definitions.note: the answer is plural, the definition singular; each base rate is a level of interest

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the foundation

parts.note: a base is a foundation

indicators.note: a rest that is disturbed is broken up, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone's rest is disturbed after laying foundations, as a banker sets interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A base rate is the rate a central bank sets for lending, the benchmark level from which other interest rates follow.

clue.text: Chained wrong anteater

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal has been wrongly tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying mammal of Australia that feeds on ants.

clue.text: Heading off, welshing maybe on old Albion supporters?

definitions.note: the English as a people, a plural noun

indicators.note: maybe hints at one possible arrangement among many, so the letters are reordered
with its heading off a word loses its first letter

parts.note: welshing is reneging on a debt or bet

explanation.surface: Fans of a football club called Albion leave early, perhaps without paying their bets.
explanation.walkthrough: Albion is an old poetic name for England, and several English football clubs carry it, such as West Bromwich Albion.
explanation.definitionFit: Albion is an ancient name for Britain, so those who back old Albion are the English.

clue.text: Take issue with new ride holding very noisy element

indicators.note: the rearranged ride holds the musical marking inside it
a new version of ride puts its letters in a new order

parts.note: ff is the musical marking fortissimo, very loud

explanation.surface: Disagreeing about a new ride with a very loud part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns RIDE into DIER, holding FF.
explanation.definitionFit: To differ with someone is to disagree, to take issue with what they say.

clue.text: Monster with a lethal stare — Herb is king!

parts.note: basil is a culinary herb
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A story about a deadly-eyed beast whose ruler turns out to be named Herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The basilisk is a legendary serpent whose gaze could kill anyone it looked at.

clue.text: In an Englishman's castle silver is protected with respect

indicators.note: something protected is shielded by walls around it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: from the proverb an Englishman's home is his castle
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: The family silver is kept safe within a proud Englishman's fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'an Englishman's home is his castle' is used in reverse: the castle stands for the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public honour or tribute paid to someone, a show of respect.

clue.text: Deem a change to be necessary for Jason's legendary assistant

indicators.note: a change alters the arrangement, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone judges that a shake-up is needed for the hero's helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A change' reads as one phrase, but its a joins the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the sorceress Medea helped Jason win the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: So half fold at sea — the result of heavy rain

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters before the indicator

explanation.surface: Instructions for folding a sail halfway while out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash flood is a sudden local inundation caused by a downpour too intense to drain.

clue.text: Stage part of Driving Miss Daisy

indicators.note: part of says only a portion of the title's letters is wanted, read in place

parts.note: the letters sit at the start of the film title's last word

explanation.surface: A stage role in the play Driving Miss Daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform for speakers, a small stage.

clue.text: A poisonous element here? It's a small world!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the toxic liquid metal, Hg
second meaning: the smallest planet in the solar system

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a small world' is the stock phrase for a chance meeting; here it is literal, a small planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury names both a toxic metallic element and the tiniest planet, nearest the Sun.

clue.text: God's pain revealed in style

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A deity's suffering is shown off with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and flair, a stylish manner.
